messages:
devon: Hey support — after today's iOS client release we started seeing a bunch of 400s from /v1/embeddings. Error in logs: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1". Happening for some users only. Any pointers?

sara: Can you paste the request body (sanitized) and the exact response? Also which model/endpoint and SDK vs raw HTTP?

devon: Raw HTTP via URLSession. Here's a stripped curl we repro locally:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"text-embed-1536","input": ["[\"Hello world\"]"] }'
```

Response: 400 with body: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1"

matt: Ah — that payload is the smoking gun. The client is sending the input as a single string that contains a JSON array (i.e. the inner array was stringified). The server treats that whole string as one input, so the produced embedding is for that string not the inner text. When downstream code expects a 1536-d vector per item, but your client then tries to collapse/reshape you get mismatch.

irene: To be explicit: endpoint accepts either a single string ("input": "text here") or an array of strings ("input": ["a","b"]). If you send "[\"a\"]" (a string that looks like an array) that's still a single string. Mobile JSON bugs often come from calling JSONSerialization.data(...) then String(data: ..., encoding: .utf8) and stuffing that into a wrapper object.

devon: Ugh that's exactly our bug — we were pre-serializing small batches for logging and accidentally passed the serialized string into the network layer. Fix is trivial but curious why only some users — maybe retry/backoff paths?

sara: Also check your Content-Type and any middleware that might re-encode bodies. If you gzipped or sent ndjson accidentally we treat differently. But your curl shows plain json.

matt: Quick repro steps for eng: 1) send single-string payload where the string is a JSON array (e.g. "[\"Hello\"]"). 2) observe response embedding length for that single item (works) but client reshape code expecting batch dims triggers dimension mismatch. 3) confirm fix by sending "input": ["Hello"] (no inner quotes) -> works.

irene: On billing: double-check retry logic — if you retry on non-4xx errors you might have doubled traffic when the client retried and the server responded quickly the second time. Also check whether your client split into per-item requests in the retry path. That explains unexpected credits usage.

support-bot: Docs ref: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/embeddings#request-format (check the examples for single vs batch).

devon: Thanks all — rolled a quick patch to stop pre-serializing and added a unit test asserting the request body type. We'll monitor for billing/latency anomalies and follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

matt: If you can share a short HAR or the URLSession code snippet (sanitized) I can add a small client-side lint rule to our DEVDX checklist to catch this pattern for future iOS releases.

devon: Will drop the snippet in a follow-up thread.
